chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, said: Sa'd ibn Abd Allah narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Abi al-Khattab narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Ismail ibn Bazi, from Ibrahim ibn Abd al-Hamid, who said: I heard Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) saying during his prostration:
"O He who is Exalted so that nothing is above Him, O He who is Near so that nothing is below Him, forgive me and my companions."

key_terms.فَلاَ شَيْءَ دُونَهُ: so that nothing is below/behind Him
key_terms.فَلاَ شَيْءَ فَوْقَهُ: so that nothing is above Him

ai.seo_question: What is the supplication recited by Imam al-Kadhim during prostration?
ai.summary: Recorded in Shaykh al-Saduq’s *al-Tawhid*, this supplication highlights the dialectic of divine transcendence (*tanzih*) and nearness (*qurb*), a core theme in Shia theology used to negate anthropomorphism while affirming God's immanence. The Imam’s invocation emphasizes that Allah’s elevation is not spatial but ontological, ensuring that His closeness does not imply physical proximity. This reflects the scholarly tradition of using concise, attribute-based du'as in sujood to reinforce monotheistic purity during worship.

en.sayed-ali-raza-rizvi: 21. My father (may Allah have mercy on him) that Sa`d ibn `Abd Allah said: Muhammad ibn AlHusayn ibn Abu al-Khattab said on the authority of Muhammad ibn Isma`il ibn Bazi, on the authority of Ibrahim ibn `Abd al-Hamid that I heard Abu al-Hasan al-Kadhim (AS) saying the following prayer while he was in prostration:
“O He who is so High that nothing is above Him! O He who is so near that nothing is without Him! Forgive me and my Companions!”
